role: math olympiad participant, coach, or knowledgeable amateur posting on the Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) forum to discuss, critique, or compare solutions to a contest problem
target: a math olympiad / contest problem and approaches to solving it
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "I was fully prepared to crank out a huge coordinate bash ... until I saw the symmetry" is an observation that evidences a 'structural-insight over brute-computation' norm without naming it; the phrase "Alternatively if you didn't see the slick solution at first you can just add up the cubes" is a suggestion that evidences a 'slick-first-fallback-computational' norm; the phrase "this is trig-bashable" is an observation that evidences a 'tool-class fit / problem-amenability-to-technique' norm; the phrase "you forgot the case n=0" is a complaint that evidences a 'completeness / case-coverage' norm
polarity_hint: AoPS posts often articulate WHY a particular approach works well or poorly. Common evaluative dimensions: ELEGANCE / NON-BASH (clean synthetic/structural argument beats long coordinate/trig/algebraic 'bash'; words like "bash", "sledgehammer", "crank out" are typically negative-polarity; "slick", "clean", "elegant", "beautiful" are typically positive). NATURALNESS / MOTIVATION (does the key insight follow naturally from the problem structure?). GENERALITY / EXTENSIBILITY (does the approach generalize?). TOOL FIT / TOOL CLASS (using only "natural" tools for the problem class; using a 'sledgehammer' like complex bashing on a simpler problem is criticized as "overkill"). RIGOR / GAP-FREENESS (missing case, unjustified step, hidden assumption, circular argument). PROBLEM QUALITY ("nice problem", "trivial", "misplaced on the test" — norms about CONTEST DESIGN, not solution quality). Self-deprecating self-reports about one's own approach ("ugh, I bashed it", "I trig-bashed it FTW") ARE norm-bearing. Bare social tokens ("+1", "thanks", "oh I see") with no judgment content should produce zero signals.
